gate_rows.evidence: Treasury filtered counted cases to payments for which the full DMF was the sole death-data source, and agencies identified the payments as improper.
The reported $113.5 million benefit is offset by $4.6 million of recurring and prorated one-time costs.

Public Law 119-77 makes full-DMF access permanent effective 2026-12-27 and requires clear and convincing death evidence plus notification of connected agencies when an erroneous death record is corrected.
The published result combines payments prevented, identified, or recovered; identification alone is not a budget effect.
Counted benefits are not allocated to owning programs, so they cannot be added independently to HLT, OAS, ISF, or other lane effects.
Recovered cash is not separated from avoided payments or mapped to appropriation refunds, fund balances, or Treasury receipt accounts.
The result covers calendar 2024; the $337 million three-year projection assumes five-percent benefit growth and is not a current-law FY2026 score.
No reviewed values cover false positives, notice, appeal outcomes, payment delay, or remediation capacity.
Effects by disability, age, income, geography, protected group, provider, grantee, and claimant are not reported.

candidate_decision.next_candidate_strategy: reopen on a published Treasury annual assessment, agency aggregate event/program/fund/cohort table, scorekeeper budget effect, or audit of correction and distribution outcomes

public_warning: Causal attribution, stated-cost netting, and permanent legal authority pass, but six accounting and beneficiary gates remain blocked. The control is implemented and promising; its $108.9 million reported net benefit is still not an additive FY2026 spending reduction or package saving.
